definitions.explanation: Done without any particular intention or deep thought. Often describes words or actions that have an unintended impact.

examples.japanese: {何気|なにげ}ない{一言|ひとこと}。
{何気|なにげ}ない{会話|かいわ}が{楽|たの}しい。
{何気|なにげ}なく{言|い}った{言葉|ことば}が{相手|あいて}を{傷|きず}つけてしまった。
examples.english: Words I said without thinking ended up hurting the other person.
examples.notes: The adverbial form {何気|なにげ}なく is very common.

notes:
FORMS:
- Adnominal: {何気|なにげ}ない + noun
- Adverbial: {何気|なにげ}なく
- Predicate: {何気|なにげ}ない (rarely used predicatively)

USAGE:
Most commonly used as a modifier before a noun ({何気|なにげ}ない{一言|ひとこと}, {何気|なにげ}ない{仕草|しぐさ}) or in the adverbial form {何気|なにげ}なく. Often implies that a casual or unthinking action had significant consequences.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {何気|なにげ}ない{一言|ひとこと}: an offhand remark
- {何気|なにげ}ない{仕草|しぐさ}: an unconscious gesture
- {何気|なにげ}ない{日常|にちじょう}: ordinary daily life
- {何気|なにげ}なく{見|み}る: to glance casually

WATCH OUT:
{何気|なにげ}に is widely used in casual speech as an adverb meaning "casually" or "actually," but it is considered nonstandard. The standard adverbial form is {何気|なにげ}なく.

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {何気|なにげ}なくなかったら
